mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 4% in prior month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signal a weakening labor market and supply-side pressure, predicting negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while INDPRO decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05) when the interaction signal is present.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in home sales (HOUST) exceeding 10% year-over-year growth predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects resilient consumer demand.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive in 70% of months with HOUST > +10% YoY (binomial test).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline of at least 2% in the Industrial Production index (INDPRO) over two consecutive months predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return due to supply-side contraction.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive when INDPRO declines for two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.5% in a month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is predicted to be negative due to market anticipation of future rate hikes.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative when CPIAUCSL surprise > +0.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.5% and a rise in manufacturing payrolls (PAYEMS) suggests labor market tightening and supports positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% and PAYEMS increases in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when the interaction signal occurs (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in retail sales (not available in the catalog; fallback: use GDPC1 as proxy for broad demand, but for supply use INDPRO) over three months predicts negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to weak demand absorption.
Note: Since no direct retail proxy is available, using INDPRO as a supply proxy for this sketch as a fallback. This demonstrates a supply effect via a demand proxy due to data constraints.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative in 80% of 3-month INDPRO declines (binomial test).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of declining inflation (CPIAUCSL < 200) and persistent low unemployment (UNRATE < 5%), the S&P 500 60-day forward return is predicted to be positive due to expectations of policy easing.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 200 and UNRATE < 5% in the current month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not positive when both CPIAUCSL < 200 and UNRATE < 5% (t-test p > 0.05).
